# dorgtr

> Generates an orthogonal matrix Q which is defined as the product of N-1.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dorgtr from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dorgtr';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dorgtr( order, uplo, N, A, LDA, TAU, strideTAU, WORK ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether the upper or lower triangle was used in DSYTRD (`'upper'` or `'lower'`) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix Q<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `TAU` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | Input array |
| ↳ `strideTAU` | `integer` | `TAU` stride length |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, N - 1)</sub> | **out** · Workspace of length at least `max(1,N-1)`; for optimum performance it should hold `(N-1)*NB` elements (`NB = 32`, the dorgql/dorgqr block size), which enables the blocked path; if `null`, a workspace of the optimal size is allocated |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A contains elementary reflectors from DSYTRD;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A contains elementary reflectors from DSYTRD.
- `N`: The order of the matrix Q. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the vectors which define the elementary reflectors, as returned by DSYTRD. On exit, the N-by-N orthogonal matrix Q.
- `TAU`: `TAU(i)` must contain the scalar factor of the elementary reflector H(i), as returned by DSYTRD.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dorgtr.strided(
    uplo,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    TAU, strideTAU, offsetTAU,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether the upper or lower triangle was used in DSYTRD (`'upper'` or `'lower'`) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix Q<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, contains the reflectors from DSYTRD; on exit, the orthogonal matrix Q |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `A` |
| `TAU` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | Scalar factors of the reflectors from DSYTRD (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideTAU` | `integer` | Stride length for `TAU` |
| ↳ `offsetTAU` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `TAU` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, N - 1)</sub> | **out** · Workspace of length at least `max(1,N-1)`; for optimum performance it should hold `(N-1)*NB` elements (`NB = 32`, the dorgql/dorgqr block size), which enables the blocked path |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WORK` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A contains elementary reflectors from DSYTRD;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A contains elementary reflectors from DSYTRD.
- `N`: The order of the matrix Q. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the vectors which define the elementary reflectors, as returned by DSYTRD. On exit, the N-by-N orthogonal matrix Q.
- `TAU`: `TAU(i)` must contain the scalar factor of the elementary reflector H(i), as returned by DSYTRD.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import dorgtr from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dorgtr';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const A = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );
const TAU = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );
const WORK = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = dorgtr( 'row-major', 'upper', N, A, N, TAU, 1, WORK );
console.log( out );

// Using the strided interface:
out = dorgtr.strided( 'upper', N, A, N, 1, 0, TAU, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DORGTR`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DORGTR generates a real orthogonal matrix Q which is defined as the product of n-1 elementary reflectors of order N, as returned by DSYTRD:

if `UPLO = 'U'`, $Q = H(n-1)$ . . . H(2) H(1),

if `UPLO = 'L'`, $Q = H(1)$ H(2) . . . H(n-1).

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
